months.strategy:
Stronger in 30 2.0.

Commercial job: Run Stronger in 30 2.0 (members-only, 1 Feb–2 Mar) as the attendance engine of Q1: late joiners in, lapsed clients back, finishers renewed at list. Valentine's pairs as the acquisition story.

Newcomer: Fashionably Late (“Missed the start? The challenge saved you a seat, and 20% off.”). The challenge creates FOMO; a scaled Rookie target and a time-boxed 20% make joining late feel like winning.

Newcomer: The Plus-One Pact (“Bring your person. You both get 20% off and a date with a trainer.”). Replaces BOGO (79–94% of BOGO buyers were existing clients and renewed at 33–53%). Pairs keep each other attending; requiring both to buy makes it pure acquisition.

Renewal: Podium Pricing (“Finish Stronger in 30 and unlock the best renewal prices before April.”). Renewers average 6.4 visits in the first half of a membership vs 2.6–3.4 for lapsers. The challenge proves the habit; Podium Pricing turns it into a 3–12 month commitment.

Renewal: Bring Your Person (“Renew, bring someone new, and you both win.”). Client referral is Kwality's third-largest lead source (231 leads since Oct-25). The renewer's reward is paid only when a new client buys, so it is acquisition spend.

Newcomer: The Second Date (“Your second class is booked before you leave. Decide fast, save 20%.”). Buyers by month-one return visits: 0 → 10.8%, 1 → 43.9%, 2 → 73.3%. The booked second class plus a closing window is the lever.

Winback: Beat Your Best (“Remember your best month? Beat it, and we'll pay for the effort.”). Personal data beats a generic offer and turns the reward into attendance, which predicts the next renewal.

Renewal: Early Bird, Golden Ticket (“Anniversary prices, one month early. Plus a golden ticket.”). In 2026 Kwality's March expiries waited for April's 25–31% codes. Near-anniversary prices on longer plans now remove the reason to wait and lift the ticket.
